summary: Adds ordinary rendered Markdown prose with the package-owned localized copy control.

evidence.sourceGrammar: The copyable container accepts ordinary Markdown plus term references and rejects block code or nested package directives, so copied visible prose has one unambiguous owner.
evidence.executionCapabilities: Trusted enhancement marks the authored content owner. The existing package copy-button factory, localized states and delegated clipboard effect select rendered innerText for prose while retaining code-specific extraction for pre blocks.
evidence.confinement: Copyable prose is part of the already confined Markdown graph and creates no path, resource, include or additional read.
evidence.offlineBehavior: Compilation and clipboard interaction use local source plus package runtime through file URLs in both formats without a service or network request.
evidence.deterministicSerialization: Markup and control identity derive only from validated source and package version. Clipboard text derives from current visible rendered prose without clocks, random IDs or author callbacks.
evidence.cspAndRuntime: The extension reuses createElement, innerText and Clipboard without innerHTML, eval, script/style input, storage, form submission, dynamic import or a new CSP source.
evidence.accessibility: Prose retains normal semantic paragraphs, links and wrapping. A native localized button supports focus, Enter and Space; success/failure is announced through its visible label.
evidence.byteAndPerformanceBudgets: One control per bounded authored container and one innerText read per explicit copy action add no listener, observer, frame or background work.
evidence.packageDependenciesAndLicenses: No dependency or license is added. The implementation composes the typed directive registry, HAST enhancement, existing package runtime/icon/localization and browser APIs.
evidence.compatibility: Existing code copying, glossary controls, Markdown rendering, Review Workspace, both output formats and CLI/ESM contracts remain valid. The directive is additive within source major 1.
